$comment: SHARED fixture. The object-key format is parsed in TWO languages --
reconcile.mjs (the queue consumer) and app.parse_object_key() (the function
that decides which tenant an R2 event belongs to). Two parsers for one format
is how the two come to disagree, and the disagreement would be a tenancy bug.
So neither is trusted to describe itself. Both read THIS file: the JS test in
reconcile.test.mjs and battery group M in tenant-isolation.sh. A case added
here is a case both must satisfy, which is the only version of 'pinned
together' that is a mechanism rather than a comment.

cases.why: THE PREFIX ITSELF IS NOT AN OBJECT. Accepting it would let a notification about a directory-shaped key be accounted as a write.
organization segment is not a uuid
world segment is not a uuid
not anchored at the start -- a key that merely CONTAINS our prefix is not one of ours
a nil-variant uuid is not a v1-v5 uuid and must not parse
uppercase uuids -- scopeForWorld lowercases, so an uppercase key was never minted by us
